the full filter: one step from a computer

Android lets an app change the screen’s own colours only after a permission given once, from a computer. With it, the filter drives the phone’s settings: grayscale, the warmest Night Light, extra dim. Without it, the app can only lay a warm, darker veil over the apps: no grayscale, and the status bar, the keyboard and the notifications keep their colours.
The grayscale is what matters most. Colours are what pull the eye and hold it on the screen; in studies, people whose screen was gray used their phone 20 to 40 minutes less a day.
